Cyclone Emeline Disrupts Economic Activity Across Mauritius

Port Louis, Mauritius – The powerful Cyclone Emeline continues to disrupt economic activity across Mauritius, as torrential rains and winds exceeding 140 km/h batter the island nation for a second day. Authorities report widespread flooding in low-lying regions, with the capital Port Louis and major industrial zones severely affected.

The Mauritius Meteorological Services has maintained a Class IV cyclone warning, the highest alert level, urging residents to remain indoors. “We are experiencing one of the most intense cyclones in recent memory,” said Dr. Rajiv Kowlessur, Director of the Meteorological Services. “The storm’s slow movement means heavy rain is expected to persist through tonight and possibly tomorrow.”

Transport and logistics have come to a near standstill. Port Louis Harbour, the country’s critical gateway for imports and exports, suspended all operations late Sunday. The main airport at Plaine Magnien remains closed, with all flights cancelled or diverted. “Our members are unable to move goods or access worksites,” said Amrita Pillay, spokesperson for the Mauritius Chamber of Commerce and Industry. “There will be immediate impacts on supply chains and exports, particularly for textiles, sugar, and seafood.”

Electricity and communications infrastructure have been hit hard. More than 70,000 households are without power, according to the Central Electricity Board. Telecom services are also experiencing outages, hindering remote work and emergency coordination.

Tourism, a pillar of the Mauritian economy, is facing significant disruption as hotels evacuate guests from coastal areas and suspend bookings. “The safety of our staff and visitors is our top priority,” stated Nilesh Ramdin, president of the Mauritius Tourism Association.

Analysts warn that the full economic impact will depend on the cyclone’s duration and the extent of infrastructure damage. “A prolonged disruption could slow GDP growth this quarter,” said economist Priya Chetty. The government has not yet released estimates of losses but has pledged swift support for affected communities and businesses.
